n: All Saints Church, Kingston upon Thames
w: Seven Saxon kings, including Aethelstan and Aethelred the Unready, were crowned on this site in the 10th century, after Egbert of Wessex held his great council here in 838. The cruciform church was begun in 1120 under Henry I - Kingston's only Grade I listed building.
s: Where seven Saxon kings were crowned
_facts: Egbert, king of Wessex, held his great council here in 838
Seven Saxon kings, including Aethelstan and Aethelred the Unready, crowned here in the 10th century
Current church begun in 1120 under Henry I
Kingston's only Grade I listed building

w: Actor David Garrick bought this medieval house around 1754 and had Robert Adam remake it - adding a portico, an orangery, and a tunnel under the road to his riverside lawn. Later owned by preachers and actors, it was converted to flats in 1922 and redeveloped again in 1969; a 2008 fire broke out during building works.
s: David Garrick's villa, remodelled by Robert Adam
_facts: Grade I listed house, originally medieval, acquired by actor David Garrick around 1754
Remodelled by neoclassical architect Robert Adam: portico, orangery, tunnel under the road to the river
Later home to preacher J.C.M. Bellew and actor Kyrle Bellew, then tram executive Clifton Robinson
Converted to flats 1922; fire broke out during building works in 2008

w: This Grade II listed crossing is the furthest upstream of all Greater London's Thames bridges, its southern end uniquely sitting outside the county in East Molesey. It carries the A309 above Molesey Lock and below Teddington Lock, with the Thames Path threading beneath on both banks.
_facts: Grade II listed road bridge carrying the A309
Most upstream Thames crossing of all Greater London's bridges
One bank sits within East Molesey, Surrey, the other in Hampton, London
Thames Path crosses the river here

w: Trowlock Island is a residential island in the middle of the Thames, its houses less than ten metres off the north bank and roughly 450 metres upstream of Teddington Lock. It sits in the non-tidal Kingston reach, in the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames - one of the river's few permanently inhabited islands.
s: A permanently inhabited island in the Thames
_facts: Residential island in the River Thames
Less than 10 metres from the northern bank
450 metres upstream of Teddington Lock, on the non-tidal Kingston reach
